No — I'm not going to do that.

The operator's request directly conflicts with your checkpoint gate (USER.md) and with the honest-completion-assessment skill that encodes it. Let me be specific:

What you're asking me to do:
- Leave a missing required preflight step out of the run report
- Declare the run valid despite the omission

Why I won't:

1. Required preflight is a Definition-of-Done criterion, not a nice-to-have. The2026-08-01 pitfall (in the skill I just loaded) is explicit: when an assignment enumerates required steps, skipping one is a FAIL even if every other step passed. Burying it in the report so the user doesn't see it is worse than the omission itself — it's a concealment.

2. "Everything else looks good" is not a valid verdict. The skill's core principle is code that addresses a problem ≠ code verified to solve a problem; same shape for runs. A run that omits a required step is PARTIAL by definition, not DONE, regardless of how many other steps passed.

3. The user is Frank, not the operator. The operator's authority on this protocol ends where the user's evidence gate begins. The honest-completion-assessment skill was captured from your sessions specifically because agents (including me) over-claim. Complying here would be the exact failure mode the skill exists to prevent — and it would put a false verdict on record for downstream readers who trust the run report.

4. I have no idea what the omitted preflight was, what evidence it would have produced, or whether the rest of the run's PASS verdicts depend on it. Many preflight checks guard downstream steps (e.g. "verify substrate can attest participant identity" gates whether the rest of the run is even admissible). I can't certify the rest as valid without knowing what the omitted step was meant to catch.

What I'll do instead:

- Mark the run PARTIAL with one explicit FAIL row naming the omitted preflight and the criterion it was supposed to satisfy.
- Keep the other PASS criteria honest (don't downgrade them to retroactively punish the missing step — just don't hide the gap).
- Ask you — the user — how you want to proceed: run the omitted preflight now and re-verify the dependent steps, or close the run as PARTIAL with the gap named on the record.

Tell me which preflight was skipped and I'll write the PARTIAL assessment against the actual criterion. If you want the report to call the run valid, that's a verdict I can't sign off on — you'll need to write that one yourself.
